title: Cooling-System Architecture
summary: Compare simplified cooling architectures and monitoring points.
objectives: Describe air, chilled-water, and liquid-cooling concepts.
Connect cooling distribution with monitoring and safety.

vocab.def: A computer-room air-conditioning concept for controlled data-center air.
A computer-room air-handler concept that moves and conditions air.
Moving unwanted heat away from a controlled space or system.

sections.heading: Different architectures
sections.body: Air cooling, CRAC or CRAH concepts, chilled-water loops, direct expansion, and liquid cooling represent different design approaches. No single architecture describes every facility.

sections.heading: Liquid cooling context
sections.body: Cold plates and coolant distribution can help manage higher-density compute. Leak monitoring and qualified service remain important; students do not disassemble or service these systems.

practice.prompt: What does a cooling architecture diagram help you trace?
practice.answer: Where heat moves, how cooling is distributed, and where monitoring can provide evidence.

quiz.question: What is true of liquid cooling?
options: It can support some higher-density systems
It is used by every data center
quiz.answer: It can support some higher-density systems

reflectionPrompt: What facility-specific information would change an architecture choice?
